channel.description: Latest articles from CT News Junkie (ctnewsjunkie.com)

item.title: Lamont Pitches CT Gas Tax Holiday As War Drives Prices Higher
item.description: In an event at a family-owned fuel company, Gov. Ned Lamont pitched a gas tax holiday Tuesday as a short-term answer to rising fuel prices as a result of the U.S. and Israel - Iran war. He estimated the move would save drivers about a quarter per gallon, or about $20 a month for someone who uses 20 gallons a week.

item.title: Republicans Cry Foul Over Public Hearing Time Limit As Committees Debate Vaccine, Homeschooling Bills
item.description: The Education Committee, which scheduled a public hearing on a public education equivalence bill that opponents said unfairly targeted homeschoolers, had also announced a time limit, but had rescinded the limit before convening the hearing.

item.title: CT Joins Lawsuit Over Federal Demands For College Admissions Survey Data
item.description: The purpose of this new survey is to track institutions’ compliance with the Supreme Court decision in Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard, which says that race cannot be used as a factor in admissions.

item.title: Lamont, 18 Other Governors Urge Congress To Rein In Tariffs
item.description: In their letter, the governors expressed concern for residents in their respective states, who “have experienced significant economic harm as a result of the sweeping tariffs imposed by the Executive Branch this past year.”

item.title: Correction Dept. Investigating After Suspect Dies In Custody
item.description: According to the department, correctional and medical staff at the facility responded to an emergency medical code shortly after midnight on March 12.

item.title: License Plate Reader Bill Likely To Pass This Session, CT Senator Says
item.description: Dozens of residents and some law enforcement officers provided testimony on House Bill 5449, An Act Concerning Automated License Plate Reader Systems, during the Judiciary Committee’s public hearing this week.

item.title: CT Consumer Counsel: Yankee Gas Rate Increase Another Setback For Connecticut Customers
item.description: Yankee Gas customers will have to pay an additional 75 cents per month over and above the original $15 rate hike in the average residential monthly bill that was a result of the first decision issued by the Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (PURA) in November, according to estimates released by Consumer Counsel Claire Coleman’s office.

item.title: Ranked Choice Voting Proposal Clears Committee
item.description: On the day Senate Bill 386, which would allow municipalities to voluntarily adopt ranked choice voting in party caucuses and primaries and some municipal elections, cleared the Government Administration and Elections Committee, a group of municipal leaders wrote to Gov. Ned Lamont and legislative leaders urging its passage into law.

item.title: CT has Erased 150,000 Criminal Records. Many Residents May Not Know.
item.description: Connecticut has automatically erased more than 150,000 criminal records under the state’s Clean Slate law, but many of the people whose convictions were wiped away may not know it.
